decision: PER-FEATURE introduces (not plan-level), per operator preference. Plan-level declaration would let any feature lean on any introduced symbol regardless of order, erasing the dependency signal the lint exists to protect. Per-feature + plan-order resolution keeps the rule honest: a feature may use symbols introduced by itself or earlier features, never by a later one.

Sequence (operator): 007 -> main FIRST; THEN this precursor (small, lock/build/merge) because plan 2026-06-07-001 cannot lock until it exists; THEN Plan A lock/build; THEN 008. This is a real DontPanic governance improvement (greenfield/contract plans were structurally unlockable), not a one-off unblock. Drafted on branch fix/plan-review-introduces-vocabulary off main, doc-only, status:draft.

This precursor plan is itself self-lockable WITHOUT the affordance it adds: the coupling lint only extracts snake_case/dotted tokens, so the bare word 'introduces' is not flagged, and the ACs reference only symbols that already exist in plan_review (missing_prereq, plan-review). The ACs deliberately avoid naming non-existent snake_case example symbols (source_kind etc.) — that is precisely why Plan A (which MUST name them for contract precision) cannot lock and this fix is needed. NOTE: the introduces field cannot be dogfooded in this plan's own features.json yet — the strict Features Pydantic model forbids extra keys (extra_forbidden), which F001 must widen; dogfooding lands after F001.
